display_name: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV & Sir M. Visvesvaraya
one_line: The Maharaja of Mysore and his Dewan, building a model state through education, industry and administration.

appearance.age_look: early 40s for Krishnaraja, late 40s–50s for Visvesvaraya; both slim, upright builds with a composed, scholarly air
appearance.face: Krishnaraja: oval face, medium-brown Mysore complexion, neat trimmed moustache, calm thoughtful eyes with a gentle default half-smile; Visvesvaraya: longer face, slightly lighter brown, angular nose, thin lips, small tidy moustache, default expression focused and serious.
appearance.hair: Krishnaraja: short, well-groomed black hair mostly hidden under a deep-maroon Mysore-style velvet turban with a central white plume and a small gold sarpech; Visvesvaraya: mostly concealed hair under a tall white Mysore Iyengar-style turban (peta) with simple folds and no ornament.
appearance.costume: Krishnaraja wears an early-20th-century Mysore royal achkan: a long, high-collared sherwani-style coat in rich ivory silk with subtle vertical jacquard texture, reaching just below the knees, fastened with small gold buttons, over a deep-maroon silk angavastram draped neatly over the left shoulder and across the torso; he has straight white churidar trousers, and simple polished brown leather shoes; across his chest is a single dark-green silk sash symbolising state service, with a modest round gold badge at the left; minimal jewellery: a thin gold chain partly visible at the collar and a simple gold ring on his right hand. Visvesvaraya wears a practical yet dignified administrator’s outfit: a plain, well-pressed off-white cotton long-coat (closed-band collar, length to mid-thigh) over a pale-grey high-collared waistcoat and crisp white kurta, with matching white dhoti neatly pleated and brought up to the ankles, and black leather lace-up shoes; he carries a small pocket watch chain on his waistcoat and has a folded light-grey wool shawl over his left forearm, hinting at long hours of inspection and planning.
appearance.signature: A shared large, rolled parchment blueprint tied with a dark-green ribbon, held between them: on one side faintly visible line-work of a factory with a tall chimney and gears, and on the other side a stylised university building façade with an arched entrance and domed tower, symbolising their joint planning of institutions, while Krishnaraja also wears a small leather-bound ledger tucked under his right arm and Visvesvaraya holds a slim metal engineer’s scale in his left hand resting against the blueprint.

ref_desc: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV and M. Visvesvaraya stand together, with Krishnaraja in an ivory silk achkan, deep-maroon turban and green sash, Visvesvaraya in off-white long-coat, white dhoti and plain white turban, both holding a shared rolled institutional blueprint accented by dark green details.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV and Sir M. Visvesvaraya together as one iconic duo from early 20th-century Mysore: Krishnaraja is a slim, dignified Maharaja with an oval, medium-brown face, neat moustache and calm eyes, wearing a rich ivory silk achkan with subtle vertical texture, small gold buttons, a deep-maroon silk angavastram over the left shoulder, a dark-green silk sash with a round gold badge across his chest, white churidar trousers and polished brown leather shoes; he has short black hair mostly hidden by a deep-maroon Mysore-style velvet turban with a central white plume and a small gold sarpech, and minimal jewellery, plus a small leather-bound ledger tucked under his right arm. Beside him, Visvesvaraya is a slightly older, angular-faced administrator with a focused expression, light-brown complexion and small moustache, wearing a tall plain white Mysore Iyengar-style turban, a well-pressed off-white cotton long-coat over a pale-grey high-collared waistcoat and crisp white kurta, a neatly pleated white dhoti to the ankles, black leather lace-up shoes, and a light-grey wool shawl folded over his left forearm; a pocket watch chain is visible on his waistcoat. Between them they hold a single large rolled parchment blueprint tied with a dark-green ribbon, with faint line-work suggesting both a factory with a chimney and a university building façade with an arched entrance, and Visvesvaraya also rests a slim metal engineer’s scale against the blueprint; keep the palette to deep maroon, ivory, dark green, off-white and light grey, and present them front-facing with consistent facial features, hair, costumes and props so they can be redrawn identically in different panels.
